paragraphs: Clearview AI sells facial recognition software that law enforcement agencies use to generate leads and identify suspects, witnesses and victims. The company states its mission as reducing crime, fraud and risk, and it also points the technology at national security and military defense. Development is U.S.-based, the site says, with certification for data security and cybersecurity policies.

The company states that its law enforcement database holds more than 70 billion images. It says the model was trained on the largest and most diverse dataset. The homepage adds that the algorithm has been tested by NIST and performs in challenging photographic conditions. In a company blog post, Clearview says its algorithm achieved greater than 99 percent accuracy across all demographics in NIST's 1:1 FRVT test.

Success stories listed on the site include the Miami Police Department locating a fleeing homicide suspect. Another describes the Hernando County Sheriff's Office solving a case the company says could have gone cold. A press release dated July 1, 2026 announces that Clearview GovCloud reached FedRAMP In Process designation at the High Impact Level. Another, dated August 11, 2026, notes a third consecutive year on the Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies.
